newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq has no plans to change dinar - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Iraq has no plans to change dinar - central bank.

text.p: Iraq has no plans to change its currency and the dinar is expected to gain against the dollar in the coming days, the governor of Iraq's central bank said in remarks published on Wednesday.

"There has been a circulation of rumours that the (Iraqi) currency would be changed and a zero would be dropped (from bank notes)...The central bank has refuted such baseless rumours in more than one occasion," Isam Hweish told the official weekly magazine Alef-Ba.

Iraq's limited oil exports, which started two weeks ago under an oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations, had more than doubled the value of the dinar, moving from 1,650 to the dollar before oil exports to a high of 700.

But the battered currency, which has plummmeted in value under the U.N. trade sanctions imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, slumped again to 1,100 dinars to one dollar over the last two weeks on fears the government may change it.
Under the deal signed on May 20, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicine for the Iraqi population.
Hweish expected the value of the dinar to soar during the next few days when foodstuffs bought by Iraq under the pact start arriving in the country.
"The value of the dollar would slip (against the dinar) during the coming days with the start of the distribution of food imported under the memorandum of understanding," he said.
The governor did not rule out measures by the central bank to improve the Iraqi volatile currency.
"It is not only that the central bank buys and sells foreign currency, there are other measures," he said without elaboration.
